facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The financial base is a consolidated, USD, filed-statement base from the 10-K and the June 30, 2026 10-Q, with company releases used only as attributed support. On the company's adjusted operating income (AOI, a non-GAAP measure that adds back share-based compensation, depreciation and amortization, restructuring, impairment and cloud computing amortization and adds the proportionate AOI of majority-owned equity investees) the twelve months to June 30, 2026 produced 313,045 against 411,874 for FY2025. Total debt principal fell from 1,778,251 to 1,735,554 and cash from 502,379 to 463,996, so net debt was 1,275,872 and then 1,271,558. The result is gross debt to AOI of 5.54x and net debt to AOI of 4.06x at June 30, 2026, against 4.32x and 3.10x at FY2025, with AOI to cash interest paid of 2.07x against 2.63x. These ratios use the AOI definition and are not the credit-agreement ratios, which were last reported at March 31, 2026 (net leverage 5.11x against a 5.75x maximum that applied through March 31, 2026 and steps down to 5.50x after; interest coverage 1.85x against a 1.50x minimum) and ended with the facility on May 12, 2026. Using reported operating income plus depreciation and amortization, with no add-backs, the same debt gives much higher multiples because the twelve-month windows include a non-cash impairment charge of 97,784 recorded in Q4 2025; both bases are shown in the calculations and the chart rows use the AOI basis. The base supports the report's leverage, cover, liquidity and maturity charts for three period ends, with the limits listed under Gaps.

facts.label: Definitions and comparability
facts.text: - AOI. Defined in the segment note as operating income before depreciation and amortization, cloud computing amortization, share-based compensation, impairment and other charges, restructuring and other related charges, and including the proportionate share of adjusted operating income of majority-owned equity method investees (10-Q Q2-26 page:28). It is a segment measure and a non-GAAP total; it is not EBITDA. Three consequences: it excludes restructuring cash costs (cash paid for restructuring initiatives was 19,729 in 6M 2026 against 7,920 in 6M 2025, Rel Jul page:11), it adds back equity-classified and some other share-based compensation, and it adds investee AOI that is not consolidated cash flow (6,762 in 6M 2026). - EBITDA on a reported basis. Operating income plus depreciation and amortization, with no add-backs. The twelve-month windows to March 31 and June 30, 2026 include the Q4 2025 non-cash impairment and other charges of 97,784 (10-K page:134; Q4 2025 timing per 10-Q Q2-26 page:16), so this basis understates run-rate earnings; it is shown in C7 for transparency, not charted. - Net debt. Principal of debt less cash and cash equivalents, no restricted cash adjustment (none is printed), no lease adjustment. The company's own leverage ratio (3.1x at FY2025, 3.4x at March 31, 2026, 4.1x at June 30, 2026) divides net debt and finance leases by AOI (Rel Feb page:11, Rel May page:9, Rel Jul page:11); the difference from C3 is the finance lease liability (13,882 at June 30, 2026, Rel Jul page:11). - Credit-agreement ratios. Company-reported at December 31, 2025 and March 31, 2026 only; they follow credit-agreement definitions that differ from AOI and ended with the facility on May 12, 2026 (10-Q Q2-26 page:17). The remaining notes' covenants are not printed.

facts.label: Earnings and operating drivers
facts.text: - Revenue fell to 547,495 in Q2 2026 from 600,024 in Q2 2025 (10-Q Q2-26 page:3). Subscription revenue fell from 367,428 to 352,514, advertising from 148,609 to 138,212 and content licensing and other from 83,987 to 56,769 (page:28-29). Management attributes the licensing decline mainly to delivery timing and to a music catalog sale and Silo production revenue in Q2 2025, and says it expects licensing revenue to vary through 2026 (page:44). It expects linear subscriber declines to continue and advertising to continue to decline (page:43-44). - Operating income fell from 64,469 to 15,854 (page:3); the filing attributes this mainly to the 52.5 million revenue decrease (page:47). Domestic segment AOI fell from 126,339 to 60,972 while International was stable at 14,359 against 14,737 (page:28-29). - Cost lines did not fall with revenue: technical and operating expenses rose from 283,876 to 288,781 and selling, general and administrative expenses from 221,704 to 224,698 (page:3). - FY2025 earnings were helped by a gain on extinguishment of debt of 129,800 (10-K page:134) and hurt by the impairment of 97,784; Q2 2026 includes a loss on extinguishment of debt of 3,784 (page:3). Net income including noncontrolling interests was a loss of 36,929 in 6M 2026 against a profit of 74,859 in 6M 2025.

facts.label: Liquidity and refinancing
facts.text: - Liquidity at June 30, 2026 is cash of 463,996 (about $136.5 million held by foreign subsidiaries, of which about $22.5 million is expected to be repatriated; 10-Q Q2-26 page:55). The $175.0 million revolver and the Term Loan A were repaid or terminated on May 12, 2026 (page:17), so no committed facility remains in the sources. Management points to cash, operating cash flow, the receivables monetization program and new debt as sources (page:55); the program had no receivables sold and a limit of $125.0 million (page:10). - Management states that it does not expect to generate enough cash from operations, with cash on hand, to repay all debt at maturity and will depend on capital markets access (page:55-56). - In the 2026 exchange, about $830.6 million of 10.25% notes were tendered early and about $30.7 million at expiry (about $861.3 million together, sum of the printed amounts) for new 10.50% notes due 2032 of about $884 million and about $31.1 million (about $915.1 million together) (page:18); the remaining 13.7 million was redeemed April 6, 2026 at 105.125% (page:19). The extra principal of $53.8 million over the exchanged amount is a non-cash discount; third-party fees of $16.7 million were expensed in Miscellaneous, net (page:18). - Off-balance sheet contractual obligations rose by $91.3 million to $590.3 million at June 30, 2026, mainly marketing and third-party service contracts (page:24). - A customer filed for Chapter 11 on June 30, 2026; the filing does not name the customer or state the exposure (page:57).

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: AMC Global Media is a holding company that owns and operates linear cable networks (AMC, We TV, BBC America, IFC, SundanceTV), a portfolio of subscription streaming services (AMC+, Acorn TV, Shudder, Sundance Now, ALLBLK, HIDIVE, All Reality), a studio that owns much of its scripted content and a film distribution arm, plus an international channels business. Revenue comes from per-subscriber affiliate fees and streaming subscriptions, advertising sold on ratings guarantees, and content licensing that is lumpy by delivery timing. The business is controlled by the Dolan family group through a dual-class structure, not by a financial sponsor, so the sponsor-behaviour lens is applied to documented issuer actions only. The credit-relevant history is a sequence of liability-management steps: repurchases and a tender of the 4.25% senior notes and a new 10.50% secured issue in 2025, purchase of the remaining minority interests in BBC America and RLJ Entertainment in 2024 and 2025, an exchange of the 10.25% secured notes into the 10.50% notes in March 2026, an indenture consent that widened the buyback covenant, and in May 2026 the repayment of the Term Loan A and termination of the revolver. The creditor view is that the maturity profile has been pushed out while earnings and liquidity buffers have narrowed (CP-1 C3), that the remaining protections sit in indentures this source set does not contain, and that a pending damages claim and a streaming licence with Netflix are the main identified swing factors after June 30, 2026. The evidence is strong for facts stated in the filings and weak where it depends on management expectations or on documents not supplied.

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 1. Revenue durability. Evidence: Domestic subscription revenue is declining on basic subscriber losses, advertising is lower on ratings and pricing, and content licensing fell by 32.4% in Q2 2026 on delivery timing (10-Q Q2-26 page:42-44); management expects linear subscriber and advertising declines to continue. Risk mechanic: technical and operating and selling, general and administrative costs rose while revenue fell (10-Q Q2-26 page:3), so the revenue loss fell through to operating income (page:47). Credit implication: debt service depends on streaming growth, price increases and licensing, which are less predictable; the Netflix licence adds expected cash of about $25 million in 2026 and about $100 million a year in 2027 to 2030 but is Management Language and the contract is not supplied. Countering item: none logged as a conflict. 2. Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: Q2 2026 operating income fell from 64,469 to 15,854 on a revenue decrease of 52.5 million (10-Q Q2-26 page:47); twelve-month AOI of 313,045 against cash interest paid of 151,153 gives 2.07x cover (CP-1 C4). Mechanic: fixed programming and marketing cost base with falling revenue compresses cover; the run-rate contractual coupon on notes outstanding is 155,955 (CP-1 C8). Implication: limited tolerance for further earnings decline before leverage and cover weaken; the net debt to AOI ratio was 4.06x at June 30, 2026 (CP-1 C3). 3. Concentration. Evidence: few distributors hold a concentration of subscribers; two customers were 13% and 10% of receivables at December 31, 2025 (10-K page:146-147); a customer filed for Chapter 11 on June 30, 2026 and sought authority to pay prepetition ordinary-course claims for which the company is named as a vendor (10-Q Q2-26 page:57). Mechanic: renewal repricing and counterparty failure hit revenue and receivables together. Implication: receivables of 547,187 at June 30, 2026 (10-Q Q2-26 page:2) are exposed to counterparty events; exposure to the filing customer is Insufficient Information. 4. Sponsor and control alignment. Evidence: family control and ownership of all Class B stock (10-K page:72-73); the 2032 indenture was amended to allow buybacks up to $50.0 million, and 30,000 of treasury stock was bought in six months 2026 (10-Q Q2-26 page:6, 17), with $87 million of authorization remaining (Rel Jul page:4). Mechanic: controlled equity can direct cash to buybacks within indenture capacity at the expense of debt reduction or liquidity. Implication: monitoring item for restricted payment capacity; the gap between the $87 million board authorization and the $50.0 million indenture basket as summarised is not resolved by the sources because other baskets may apply. 5. Refinancing. Evidence: no debt due before February 2029 when 420,456 of unsecured 4.25% notes mature, and 1,315,098 of secured notes in July 2032; management states cash flow and cash will not repay all maturities and the company depends on capital markets access (10-Q Q2-26 page:55-56). Mechanic: the unsecured notes mature ahead of the secured notes; refinancing the earlier maturity depends on earnings stabilising. Implication: refinancing risk is deferred, not removed; the revolving facility's absence removes a bridge. 6. Key uncertainty: litigation. Evidence: plaintiffs claim damages in excess of $200 million in the MFN Litigation; summary judgment motion was filed; trial rescheduled to October 27, 2026; the company believes the claims are without merit and no determination of outcome can be made (10-Q Q2-26 page:24-25). Mechanic: an adverse result would be a cash claim against liquidity of cash 463,996 with no revolver. Implication: unquantified event risk dated before the as-of date with no outcome supplied; no loss estimate is recorded in the pages read.

rows.label: A family-controlled cable and streaming programmer whose linear affiliate and advertising revenue is shrinking, and whose debt was just refinanced. The 2026 exchange pushed secured maturities to 2032; control and buybacks remain creditor-relevant.
The Dolan family group controls all Class B stock and about 79% of voting power outside director elections.
The 2026 exchange moved 10.25% secured notes due 2029 into 10.50% secured notes due 2032 and redeemed the rest.
The bank facilities ended in May 2026, and buybacks continue under an amended covenant.
Revenue depends on distributors and on advertising that management expects to keep declining, with licensing uneven.
A damages claim above 200 million had a trial set for October 27, 2026; no outcome is supplied.
Revenue stream: content licensing and other
Pricing and unit economics: churn, ARPU, subscriber acquisition cost
Indentures for the 2032 secured notes, the 4.25% senior notes and the 4.25% convertible notes
Covenant certificate or compliance computation for the surviving notes
Instrument-level debt and maturity schedule in the latest 10-Q

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: 1. Earnings, not debt, drove the rise in leverage. Net debt moved from USD 1,275.9 million at December 31, 2025 to USD 1,271.6 million at June 30, 2026, while adjusted operating income over twelve months fell to USD 313.0 million from USD 411.9 million, taking net debt to adjusted operating income to 4.06x from 3.10x and total debt to adjusted operating income to 5.54x from 4.32x [CP-1 C3]. The fall came mainly from Domestic Operations, whose segment adjusted operating income was USD 61.0 million in Q2 2026 against USD 126.3 million in Q2 2025 as subscription, advertising and content licensing revenue all fell [CP-1 table; CP-1A operating model]. Management expects linear subscriber and advertising declines to continue, so the denominator carries more risk than the numerator. 2. Cash interest cover is thinner. Adjusted operating income covered cash interest paid 2.07x in the twelve months to June 30, 2026 against 2.63x in FY2025 [CP-1 C4]. Run-rate contractual coupon on the notes outstanding at June 30, 2026 is USD 156.0 million, which on the same earnings gives 2.01x [CP-1 C8]. On operating income plus depreciation and amortization with no add-backs, total debt is 12.66x earnings, but that basis includes a USD 97.8 million non-cash impairment and is shown only to expose the gap to the adjusted measure [CP-1 C7]. 3. Liquidity is cash only. The company repaid the remaining Term Loan A and terminated the USD 175.0 million revolver on May 12, 2026, leaving cash of USD 464.0 million at June 30, 2026, of which about USD 136.5 million is held by foreign subsidiaries [CP-1 liquidity rows]. The unused USD 125.0 million receivables sale program is not a committed facility. This replaces a position where cash of USD 502.4 million was backed by USD 175.0 million undrawn at December 31, 2025. 4. The maturity profile is long but ordered against unsecured holders. After the March 2026 exchange, USD 420.5 million of 4.25% unsecured senior and convertible notes mature in February 2029 ahead of USD 1,315.1 million of 10.50% secured notes in July 2032 [CP-1 C11; CP-1A transactions]. Management states that cash and operating cash flow will not repay all debt at maturity and that it depends on capital markets access. Whether the 2032 indenture constrains refinancing the earlier notes is Insufficient Information. 5. Cash flow remains positive after capital spending, but is weaker. Free cash flow was USD 108.1 million in six months 2026 against USD 189.9 million in six months 2025, and USD 190.5 million over twelve months [CP-1 C5]. Debt principal has fallen by USD 633.8 million since December 31, 2024 [CP-1A calculations], largely through discounted repurchases, a tender and Term Loan A repayments. 6. Control and capital allocation matter to creditors. The Dolan family group owns all Class B stock and about 79% of voting power outside director elections, and the company bought back USD 30.0 million of stock in six months 2026 under an indenture amendment that allows up to USD 50.0 million of equity repurchases, with USD 87 million of board authorization remaining at June 30, 2026 [CP-1A governance]. Restricted payment capacity beyond the summarised amendment is Insufficient Information. 7. Two dated events sit after the balance sheet or before an unreported outcome. The Netflix licence of July 30, 2026 brings USD 500 million of fees, with management expecting about USD 25 million of cash in 2026 and about USD 100 million a year in 2027 to 2030; and a damages claim above USD 200 million had a trial set for October 27, 2026 with no outcome supplied [CP-1 subsequent events; CP-1A credit translations]. Neither is in June 30, 2026 balances, and both are limited by documents not supplied.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. First, the company has no debt maturing before February 2029 and its secured notes run to July 2032, after it exchanged USD 861.3 million of 2029 secured notes (tagged Documentary Fact; basis maturity rows and the 2026 transaction summary). Second, it generates cash: USD 190.5 million of free cash flow over twelve months to June 30, 2026 and cash of USD 464.0 million, with total debt principal USD 633.8 million lower than at December 31, 2024 (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1 C5 and CP-1A calculations). Third, it owns a large share of its scripted content and franchises, and has licensed the Walking Dead Universe to Netflix for USD 500 million of fees over five years; the licence terms are Management Language and the contract is not supplied (basis CP-1A operating model and subsequent events). Fourth, its documented behaviour towards debt has been supportive: it repurchased and tendered senior notes at discounts in 2025 and repaid its Term Loan A (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1A governance table). Fifth, reporting quality is high, with an unqualified audit opinion and effective internal control over financial reporting for FY2025 (Documentary Fact).

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. First, earnings are falling: Q2 2026 revenue was USD 547.5 million against USD 600.0 million and operating income USD 15.9 million against USD 64.5 million, while operating cost lines rose (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1 table). Second, leverage and cover have weakened to 5.54x total and 4.06x net on adjusted operating income, and 2.07x cash interest cover (Analyst Interpretation of CP-1 C3 and C4; the adjusted measure adds back restructuring and share-based compensation). Third, there is no committed back-up facility, and the company states it depends on capital markets to refinance (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1 liquidity rows and CP-1A refinancing translation). Fourth, the earlier maturity is the junior one: USD 420.5 million of unsecured notes fall due in February 2029 ahead of the secured notes (Analyst Interpretation). Fifth, revenue is exposed to a few distributors and to advertising and subscriber declines that management expects to continue, and a customer filed for Chapter 11 on June 30, 2026 with exposure not stated (Documentary Fact for the filing; Insufficient Information for the exposure). Sixth, controlled equity, USD 30.0 million of buybacks and USD 87 million of authorization remaining while earnings fall (Documentary Fact; the creditor effect is Analyst Interpretation). Seventh, the unresolved damages claim above USD 200 million against cash of USD 464.0 million (Documentary Fact; the outcome is Insufficient Information). Eighth, ranking and collateral for the 2032 notes cannot be settled because the filing describes the guarantees as unsecured while the notes are secured by a first-priority lien (Insufficient Information; no recovery conclusion is drawn).

facts.label: Defects found, stated plainly
facts.text: - The credit synthesis says buybacks of USD 30.0 million were made under the amended covenant (reader summary and risk table). The filings state the amendment (up to $50.0 million of equity repurchases, 10-Q Q2-26 page:17) and the purchase (treasury stock 30,000, page:6; accelerated share repurchase of $30 million, Rel Jul page:4) but not that one used the other. The business handoff keeps capacity and action in separate columns and is the correct wording. - The credit synthesis calls the 4.25% notes "junior" to the secured notes while also saying ranking cannot be settled. The label rests on the instrument names (Senior Notes against Senior Secured Notes) and the 10-K description of the senior notes as guaranteed on a senior unsecured basis (10-K page:175); the guarantee wording for the secured notes is also "unsecured" (10-K page:112). The label is an Analyst Inference, not a traced ranking. - The financial base labels its chart columns "EBITDA" while using adjusted operating income, a company non-GAAP measure that adds back share-based compensation, restructuring and impairment and adds the proportionate AOI of majority-owned equity investees (10-Q Q2-26 page:28). The handoff discloses this in every basis cell, so the defect is one of label drift, not of lineage. - The business handoff attributes a 32.4% content licensing decline to delivery timing; 32.4% is the consolidated decline (10-Q Q2-26 page:42), and the timing explanation is given for the Domestic segment's 33.7% decline (page:44). Minor. - The business handoff states that the accelerated share repurchase of $30 million is the same amount as the 30,000 of treasury stock bought; the filings do not state this, but the equity statement shows treasury stock acquired of 30,137 including excise tax (10-Q Q2-26 page:4), which is consistent. Minor Analyst Interpretation.

On the company's adjusted operating income (AOI, a non-GAAP measure that adds back share-based compensation, depreciation and amortization, restructuring, impairment and cloud computing amortization and adds the proportionate AOI of majority-owned equity investees) the twelve months to June 30, 2026 produced 313,045 against 411,874 for FY2025. ### Definitions and comparability

- **AOI.** Defined in the segment note as operating income before depreciation and amortization, cloud computing amortization, share-based compensation, impairment and other charges, restructuring and other related charges, and including the proportionate share of adjusted operating income of majority-owned equity method investees (10-Q Q2-26 page:28). It is a segment measure and a non-GAAP total; it is not EBITDA. Three consequences: it excludes restructuring cash costs (cash paid for restructuring initiatives was 19,729 in 6M 2026 against 7,920 in 6M 2025, Rel Jul page:11), it adds back equity-classified and some other share-based compensation, and it adds investee AOI that is not consolidated cash flow (6,762 in 6M 2026).

- **EBITDA on a reported basis.** Operating income plus depreciation and amortization, with no add-backs. The twelve-month windows to March 31 and June 30, 2026 include the Q4 2025 non-cash impairment and other charges of 97,784 (10-K page:134; Q4 2025 timing per 10-Q Q2-26 page:16), so this basis understates run-rate earnings; it is shown in C7 for transparency, not charted.

- **Net debt.** Principal of debt less cash and cash equivalents, no restricted cash adjustment (none is printed), no lease adjustment. The company's own leverage ratio (3.1x at FY2025, 3.4x at March 31, 2026, 4.1x at June 30, 2026) divides net debt and finance leases by AOI (Rel Feb page:11, Rel May page:9, Rel Jul page:11); the difference from C3 is the finance lease liability (13,882 at June 30, 2026, Rel Jul page:11).

- **Credit-agreement ratios.** Company-reported at December 31, 2025 and March 31, 2026 only; they follow credit-agreement definitions that differ from AOI and ended with the facility on May 12, 2026 (10-Q Q2-26 page:17). The remaining notes' covenants are not printed.
### Earnings and operating drivers

- Revenue fell to 547,495 in Q2 2026 from 600,024 in Q2 2025 (10-Q Q2-26 page:3). Subscription revenue fell from 367,428 to 352,514, advertising from 148,609 to 138,212 and content licensing and other from 83,987 to 56,769 (page:28-29). Management attributes the licensing decline mainly to delivery timing and to a music catalog sale and Silo production revenue in Q2 2025, and says it expects licensing revenue to vary through 2026 (page:44). It expects linear subscriber declines to continue and advertising to continue to decline (page:43-44).

- Operating income fell from 64,469 to 15,854 (page:3); the filing attributes this mainly to the 52.5 million revenue decrease (page:47). Domestic segment AOI fell from 126,339 to 60,972 while International was stable at 14,359 against 14,737 (page:28-29).
- Cost lines did not fall with revenue: technical and operating expenses rose from 283,876 to 288,781 and selling, general and administrative expenses from 221,704 to 224,698 (page:3).

- FY2025 earnings were helped by a gain on extinguishment of debt of 129,800 (10-K page:134) and hurt by the impairment of 97,784; Q2 2026 includes a loss on extinguishment of debt of 3,784 (page:3). Net income including noncontrolling interests was a loss of 36,929 in 6M 2026 against a profit of 74,859 in 6M 2025.
### Leverage, cover and cash flow

- On the AOI basis total debt to AOI rose from 4.32x at FY2025 to 5.54x at June 30, 2026 and net debt to AOI from 3.10x to 4.06x, driven by the denominator: net debt moved from 1,275,872 to 1,271,558 while twelve-month AOI fell from 411,874 to 313,045.

- Cash interest paid over the twelve months was 151,153 against AOI of 313,045, 2.07x. Interest expense in 6M 2026 was 84,012 against 85,852 a year earlier, even though the 10.50% notes now cover 1,315,098 of principal; the lower balance of the 4.25% notes and the Term Loan A offset the higher coupon (10-Q Q2-26 page:48). The full-year effect of the post-exchange structure is shown in C8.

- Operating cash flow was 124,659 in 6M 2026 against 211,596 in 6M 2025; free cash flow after capital expenditures was 108,082 against 189,926 (page:5, 64). Management states that free cash flow includes restructuring cash costs and other items that affect comparability (Rel Jul page:11). The twelve-month free cash flow of 190,523 (C5) compares with cash interest paid of 151,153.

- Uses of cash in 6M 2026 outside debt service included 30,000 for treasury stock (page:6). A further accelerated share repurchase of $30 million with final settlement expected in the fourth quarter of 2026 and $87 million of authorization remaining at June 30, 2026 are management statements (Rel Jul page:4).
### Liquidity and refinancing

- Liquidity at June 30, 2026 is cash of 463,996 (about $136.5 million held by foreign subsidiaries, of which about $22.5 million is expected to be repatriated; 10-Q Q2-26 page:55). The $175.0 million revolver and the Term Loan A were repaid or terminated on May 12, 2026 (page:17), so no committed facility remains in the sources. Management points to cash, operating cash flow, the receivables monetization program and new debt as sources (page:55); the program had no receivables sold and a limit of $125.0 million (page:10).
- Management states that it does not expect to generate enough cash from operations, with cash on hand, to repay all debt at maturity and will depend on capital markets access (page:55-56).

- In the 2026 exchange, about $830.6 million of 10.25% notes were tendered early and about $30.7 million at expiry (about $861.3 million together, sum of the printed amounts) for new 10.50% notes due 2032 of about $884 million and about $31.1 million (about $915.1 million together) (page:18); the remaining 13.7 million was redeemed April 6, 2026 at 105.125% (page:19). The extra principal of $53.8 million over the exchanged amount is a non-cash discount; third-party fees of $16.7 million were expensed in Miscellaneous, net (page:18).
- Off-balance sheet contractual obligations rose by $91.3 million to $590.3 million at June 30, 2026, mainly marketing and third-party service contracts (page:24).
- A customer filed for Chapter 11 on June 30, 2026; the filing does not name the customer or state the exposure (page:57).
### Subsequent events (after June 30, 2026, to the cutoff)

- July 30, 2026: Netflix licence agreement for co-exclusive global streaming rights to the Walking Dead Universe. Aggregate licence fee $500 million in quarterly cash installments over five years from each title's start date; expected cash of about $25 million in 2026 and about $100 million in each of 2027, 2028, 2029 and 2030, with the remainder in 2031; expected present-value revenue about $445 million; expected revenue recognition of $200 million to $225 million in each of 2026 and 2027 (10-Q Q2-26 page:10, 68; Rel Jul page:4). These are management expectations; the contract is not supplied.

- Trial in the MFN Litigation was scheduled for October 27, 2026 with plaintiffs claiming damages in excess of $200 million (10-Q Q2-26 page:24). No later source reports an outcome, and none is assumed.
- No source dated after July 30, 2026 is supplied.
### Data quality and definition risks

- Text-only extraction: the figures above were read from page text. Tables were checked against totals where the filing prints one: the June 30, 2026 debt lines add to the printed total of 1,735,554, and the twelve-month AOI rebuilds to the printed figures (C1).

- The 10-K guarantee wording ("on an unsecured basis", page:112) and the first-priority lien description for the 2032 notes (page:171) are not reconciled by the sources; this handoff makes no statement on ranking.

- Leverage is shown on the AOI basis only because it is the one non-GAAP earnings measure for which the company prints a reconciliation; it adds back items that are real cash costs (restructuring, share-based awards settled in cash for directors).
## Calculations
All amounts are USD thousands unless stated.
**C1. Twelve-month (LTM) build to June 30, 2026 = FY2025 + 6M 2026 - 6M 2025.**
- Operating income: 133,322 + 47,115 - 128,666 = 51,771 (equals Rel Jul page:11).
- Depreciation and amortization: 94,425 + 38,243 - 47,372 = 85,296 (equals Rel Jul page:11).

- AOI: 411,874 + 115,042 - 213,871 = 313,045 (equals Rel Jul page:11). For March 31, 2026: 411,874 + 68,974 - 104,485 = 376,363 (equals Rel May page:9), where 68,974 and 104,485 are the printed Q1 2026 and Q1 2025 AOI (Rel May page:10).
**C2. Twelve-month cash interest paid.**
**C3. Leverage on the AOI basis.**
- Company-style check including finance leases: June 30, 2026 net debt and finance leases 1,285,440 / 313,045 = 4.11x, which the company prints as 4.1x (Rel Jul page:11).

**C5. Cash flow.** LTM operating cash flow = 305,670 + 124,659 - 211,596 = 218,733. LTM capital expenditures = 33,303 + 16,577 - 21,670 = 28,210. LTM free cash flow = 218,733 - 28,210 = 190,523. FY2025 free cash flow = 305,670 - 33,303 = 272,367. The 6M free cash flows are printed (10-Q Q2-26 page:64).

**C6. Program rights obligations.** December 31, 2025: 258,252 (current) + 181,773 (noncurrent) = 440,025. June 30, 2026: 226,312 + 155,386 = 381,698 (10-Q Q2-26 page:2). Not included in debt, net debt or the leverage ratios.

**C7. Reported-basis EBITDA (operating income plus depreciation and amortization, no add-backs) and ratios.** FY2025: 133,322 + 94,425 = 227,747; debt 7.81x, net debt 5.60x, cover 1.45x on cash interest paid of 156,563. LTM March 2026: 100,386 + 94,922 = 195,308 (Rel May page:9); 9.37x, 6.54x, 1.24x on 157,810. LTM June 2026: 51,771 + 85,296 = 137,067; 12.66x, 9.28x, 0.91x on 151,153. These windows include the 97,784 impairment, so the multiples are shown to expose the gap between reported and adjusted earnings, not as run-rate leverage.

**C8. Run-rate contractual coupon on notes outstanding at June 30, 2026 (assumes principal at June 30, 2026 for a full year, excludes discount amortization and interest income).** 1,315,098 x 10.50% = 138,085; 276,706 x 4.25% = 11,760; 143,750 x 4.25% = 6,109; total 155,955. LTM AOI 313,045 / 155,955 = 2.01x. Coupon rates are from the instrument labels and the 10-K debt note (page:171, 175-176).

**C9. Covenant-style headroom at March 31, 2026 (last reported, facility since ended).** Net leverage: the maximum was 5.75x through March 31, 2026 (10-Q Q1-26 page:14), so 5.75x less 5.11x reported = 0.64x; the step-down to 5.50x applied after that date and would have left 0.39x on the same ratio. Interest coverage 1.85x reported less 1.50x minimum = 0.35x. No headroom is computed for June 30, 2026: Not calculable, because the credit agreement ended on May 12, 2026 and the notes' covenants are not printed.

**C10. Netflix cash timing (management expectation).** Aggregate $500 million; about $25 million in 2026 plus four years at about $100 million equals about $425 million; the remainder due in 2031 is therefore about $75 million, derived by subtraction, not printed.
**C11. Debt maturity grouping.** 2029: 276,706 + 143,750 = 420,456. 2032: 1,315,098. Total 1,735,554, equal to the printed total debt at June 30, 2026.
## Gaps
- Not supplied: any report or filing after July 30, 2026 (CP-0 L1). Q3 2026 results are not in the sources; figures here run to June 30, 2026.

- Not supplied: executed credit agreement, indentures and supplemental indentures (CP-0 L2). Covenants of the surviving notes, security package and guarantee ranking are not printed; the credit-agreement ratios cannot be extended past March 31, 2026 (CP-0 L3). Covenant headroom at June 30, 2026 is Not calculable.

- Not supplied: letters of credit drawn on the revolver before its termination; none is printed in the sources after a search for "letters of credit", "LC", "L/C", "standby" and "surety". The $175.0 million undrawn figure is therefore shown gross.
- Not supplied: a debt maturity table in the 10-Q; maturities are read from the instrument labels (final maturity month and year), and the exact day of the 4.25% Senior Notes maturity was not read.
- Not supplied: quarterly cash interest paid for Q2 2026 and Q2 2025 as printed; they can be derived from six-month less three-month amounts but are not charted.
- Not supplied: AOI for FY2024 and earlier in this handoff; not needed for the requested periods.
- Not supplied: ratings, market prices, peers, and the identity and exposure of the customer in Chapter 11 (CP-0 L7).

- Perimeter: consolidated, including non-wholly-owned entities at 100%; restricted and unrestricted subsidiary splits are Not supplied (CP-0 L5). Majority-owned equity investees AOI is included in AOI.

- Net debt excludes lease liabilities (88,600 at June 30, 2026), program rights obligations (381,698) and the 590.3 million of off-balance sheet obligations; these are shown separately and are not in any ratio.
- Extraction is text only; table alignment was checked against printed totals where available (CP-0 L8).
## Next module

Pass to CP-1A with the following carried forward: leverage and cover are on the AOI basis; the credit-agreement ratios and revolver ended on May 12, 2026; liquidity at June 30, 2026 is cash of 463,996 with no committed facility; maturities are 420,456 in February 2029 and 1,315,098 in July 2032; the Netflix licence and the October 27, 2026 trial are subsequent events with no outcome supplied. CP-2 and CP-5 should treat the C-numbered calculations here as the source of every derived figure and the CP-0 limitations L1 to L11 as still in force.

### Business and transaction view

AMC Global Media is a holding company that owns and operates linear cable networks (AMC, We TV, BBC America, IFC, SundanceTV), a portfolio of subscription streaming services (AMC+, Acorn TV, Shudder, Sundance Now, ALLBLK, HIDIVE, All Reality), a studio that owns much of its scripted content and a film distribution arm, plus an international channels business. Revenue comes from per-subscriber affiliate fees and streaming subscriptions, advertising sold on ratings guarantees, and content licensing that is lumpy by delivery timing. The business is controlled by the Dolan family group through a dual-class structure, not by a financial sponsor, so the sponsor-behaviour lens is applied to documented issuer actions only. The credit-relevant history is a sequence of liability-management steps: repurchases and a tender of the 4.25% senior notes and a new 10.50% secured issue in 2025, purchase of the remaining minority interests in BBC America and RLJ Entertainment in 2024 and 2025, an exchange of the 10.25% secured notes into the 10.50% notes in March 2026, an indenture consent that widened the buyback covenant, and in May 2026 the repayment of the Term Loan A and termination of the revolver. The creditor view is that the maturity profile has been pushed out while earnings and liquidity buffers have narrowed (CP-1 C3), that the remaining protections sit in indentures this source set does not contain, and that a pending damages claim and a streaming licence with Netflix are the main identified swing factors after June 30, 2026. The evidence is strong for facts stated in the filings and weak where it depends on management expectations or on documents not supplied.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The 2026 transaction set is a refinancing and simplification, not a cash raise. On February 23, 2026 the company launched an exchange offer for any and all of its $875 million of 10.25% Senior Secured Notes due January 2029 into additional 10.50% Senior Secured Notes due July 2032, which form part of the same series as the $400.0 million of 2032 notes issued in July 2025 (10-Q Q2-26 page:17-18). Holders tendering by March 6, 2026 received $1,065 of 2032 notes per $1,000 and later tenders $1,015; early settlement on March 13, 2026 issued about $884 million of notes against about $830.6 million tendered, and final settlement on March 25, 2026 issued about $31.1 million against about $30.7 million (page:18). The remaining 2029 notes of about $13.7 million were redeemed on April 6, 2026 at 105.125% of principal, with a $0.7 million charge (page:19). The 2032 notes outstanding are 1,315,098 (page:16). The incremental principal of $53.8 million was accounted for as a debt modification and recorded as a debt discount, and third-party exchange fees of $16.7 million were expensed in Miscellaneous, net (page:18). These are Documentary Facts. Status: completed.

In parallel, on February 23, 2026 the company received requisite consents to amend the indenture for the 2032 notes: to permit buybacks of equity interests up to an aggregate of $50.0 million, to limit transfers of certain trademarks to unrestricted subsidiaries to non-exclusive licences, and to restrict investments in unrestricted subsidiaries under the Permitted Investments definition to specified clauses; a $2.0 million consent fee was paid and capitalized (page:17). Status: effective. The legal terms themselves (definitions, baskets, ratio tests) are not supplied.

On May 12, 2026 the company repaid the $80.0 million remaining Term Loan A under the Credit Agreement and terminated the revolving credit facility, recording a $3.1 million charge (page:17; Rel Jul page:4). Status: completed. This ended the maintenance covenants of the Credit Agreement (CP-1 Gaps); no replacement committed facility is described.

The prior-year steps explain today's structure. In July 2025 the company issued $400.0 million of 10.50% secured notes due 2032 for net proceeds of $394.5 million, which with cash funded a tender of $600.0 million of 4.25% senior notes at a discount of $111.0 million and the prepayment of the remaining $70.0 million of the non-extended Term Loan A; during 2025 it also repurchased $108.3 million of senior notes in the open market at discounts of $28.2 million (10-K page:110). On October 29, 2025 Amendment No. 5 to the Credit Agreement extended $111.8 million of revolver commitments to the earlier of October 29, 2030 or 90 days before certain capital markets maturities, lowered the minimum interest coverage ratio to 1.50:1.00 and retired $165.7 million of term loans held by consenting lenders (10-K page:110-111, 169). On November 26, 2025 the company bought the remaining 17% of RLJ Entertainment for $75.0 million cash, and on November 1, 2024 the remaining 50.1% of BBC America for $42.0 million, together with a new $40.0 million program license agreement with BBC Studios (10-K page:190-191).

Use of proceeds and liquidity effect: none of the 2026 steps raised cash. Cash outflows were $82.9 million on the Term Loan A and $14.4 million on the 2029 notes redemption in six months 2026 (10-Q Q2-26 page:5), with debt principal falling to 1,735,554 and committed liquidity to nil at June 30, 2026 (CP-1 chart rows). Sponsor: none. Dividend recapitalisation: none documented; the cash flow statements show no dividend payments to stockholders in FY2025 or six months 2026 (10-K page:136; 10-Q Q2-26 page:5-6).

Analyst Interpretation: the exchange and the April 2026 redemption retired the whole 875,000 January 2029 secured maturity (about 861.3 million exchanged and about 13.7 million redeemed), extended secured debt to July 2032, and left the 4.25% unsecured senior and convertible notes of 420,456 as the next maturity in February 2029, ahead of the secured 2032 notes (CP-1 C11). The coupon on the exchanged debt rose from 10.25% to 10.50% and the principal exchanged rose by the early-tender and exchange premium. Whether the 2032 indenture restricts the company's ability to refinance the 2029 unsecured notes ahead of the secured notes is Insufficient Information, because the indenture is not supplied.

Subsequent event after June 30, 2026 and before the cutoff: the Netflix licence of July 30, 2026 (co-exclusive global streaming rights to The Walking Dead Universe; $500 million fee; expected present-value revenue about $445 million; expected recognition of $200 million to $225 million in each of 2026 and 2027) and an accelerated share repurchase of $30 million with Citibank entered on May 8, 2026 with final settlement expected in the fourth quarter of 2026 (Rel Jul page:4). These are Management Language and are not folded into June 30, 2026 balances.

- **Control (Documentary Fact).** The Dolan Family Group owns all Class B stock and about 79% of voting power outside director elections; it is able to prevent a change in control and to elect the directors chosen by Class B holders (10-K page:72-73). Class B shares are generally entitled to ten votes each (page:72). Economic interest: about 4% of Class A (page:72). Percentages for Class B beyond "all" are not inferred.

- **Convertible notes (Documentary Fact).** The 4.25% convertible notes due 2029 convert at an initial price of approximately $12.74 per Class A share (10-K page:176) and require repurchase on a fundamental change (10-K page:72); a change of control therefore triggers a put by holders of 143,750 of principal.

- **Related parties (Documentary Fact).** Ordinary-course related-party revenue and charges are small (1.2 million of revenue in each of Q2 2026 and Q2 2025, 10-Q Q2-26 page:27), and the company records income from a consulting arrangement with MSG Networks (page:27). No related-party leakage of a size relevant to creditors is documented.

- **Reporting quality (Documentary Fact).** Unqualified audit opinion and effective internal control over financial reporting for FY2025 (10-K page:131-132). Higher disclosure quality supports Medium to High evidence quality for the filed figures.

### Credit translations

1. **Revenue durability.** Evidence: Domestic subscription revenue is declining on basic subscriber losses, advertising is lower on ratings and pricing, and content licensing fell by 32.4% in Q2 2026 on delivery timing (10-Q Q2-26 page:42-44); management expects linear subscriber and advertising declines to continue. Risk mechanic: technical and operating and selling, general and administrative costs rose while revenue fell (10-Q Q2-26 page:3), so the revenue loss fell through to operating income (page:47). Credit implication: debt service depends on streaming growth, price increases and licensing, which are less predictable; the Netflix licence adds expected cash of about $25 million in 2026 and about $100 million a year in 2027 to 2030 but is Management Language and the contract is not supplied. Countering item: none logged as a conflict.

2. **Margin and cash-flow risk.** Evidence: Q2 2026 operating income fell from 64,469 to 15,854 on a revenue decrease of 52.5 million (10-Q Q2-26 page:47); twelve-month AOI of 313,045 against cash interest paid of 151,153 gives 2.07x cover (CP-1 C4). Mechanic: fixed programming and marketing cost base with falling revenue compresses cover; the run-rate contractual coupon on notes outstanding is 155,955 (CP-1 C8). Implication: limited tolerance for further earnings decline before leverage and cover weaken; the net debt to AOI ratio was 4.06x at June 30, 2026 (CP-1 C3).

3. **Concentration.** Evidence: few distributors hold a concentration of subscribers; two customers were 13% and 10% of receivables at December 31, 2025 (10-K page:146-147); a customer filed for Chapter 11 on June 30, 2026 and sought authority to pay prepetition ordinary-course claims for which the company is named as a vendor (10-Q Q2-26 page:57). Mechanic: renewal repricing and counterparty failure hit revenue and receivables together. Implication: receivables of 547,187 at June 30, 2026 (10-Q Q2-26 page:2) are exposed to counterparty events; exposure to the filing customer is Insufficient Information.

4. **Sponsor and control alignment.** Evidence: family control and ownership of all Class B stock (10-K page:72-73); the 2032 indenture was amended to allow buybacks up to $50.0 million, and 30,000 of treasury stock was bought in six months 2026 (10-Q Q2-26 page:6, 17), with $87 million of authorization remaining (Rel Jul page:4). Mechanic: controlled equity can direct cash to buybacks within indenture capacity at the expense of debt reduction or liquidity. Implication: monitoring item for restricted payment capacity; the gap between the $87 million board authorization and the $50.0 million indenture basket as summarised is not resolved by the sources because other baskets may apply.

5. **Refinancing.** Evidence: no debt due before February 2029 when 420,456 of unsecured 4.25% notes mature, and 1,315,098 of secured notes in July 2032; management states cash flow and cash will not repay all maturities and the company depends on capital markets access (10-Q Q2-26 page:55-56). Mechanic: the unsecured notes mature ahead of the secured notes; refinancing the earlier maturity depends on earnings stabilising. Implication: refinancing risk is deferred, not removed; the revolving facility's absence removes a bridge.

6. **Key uncertainty: litigation.** Evidence: plaintiffs claim damages in excess of $200 million in the MFN Litigation; summary judgment motion was filed; trial rescheduled to October 27, 2026; the company believes the claims are without merit and no determination of outcome can be made (10-Q Q2-26 page:24-25). Mechanic: an adverse result would be a cash claim against liquidity of cash 463,996 with no revolver. Implication: unquantified event risk dated before the as-of date with no outcome supplied; no loss estimate is recorded in the pages read.
### Conflicts

No document conflict on a fact was found in the pages read. One unresolved wording tension is logged, not reconciled: the 10-K says the notes are guaranteed by domestic restricted subsidiaries "on an unsecured basis" (10-K page:112; repeated in 10-Q Q2-26 page:60), while the 2032 secured notes are described as secured on a first-priority basis by substantially all assets (10-K page:171). Effect: ranking and collateral coverage for the 2032 notes cannot be settled from the filings; any recovery mechanic that depends on it is withheld. A second, minor change over time is not a conflict: the MFN trial date moved from March 26, 2026 to April 21, 2026 (10-K page:188) and then to October 27, 2026 (10-Q Q2-26 page:24).

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| A refinanced but weakening credit: no debt matures before February 2029, yet earnings fell and the revolver is gone. Free cash flow and cash of USD 464.0 million support it; falling earnings and unseen indenture terms are the risks. | Medium | Indentures, ratings, the Netflix contract and any filing after July 30, 2026 are not supplied. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Adjusted operating income for the twelve months to June 30, 2026 was USD 313.0 million against USD 411.9 million in FY2025. | Net debt to adjusted operating income rose to 4.06x from 3.10x while net debt was flat. | High |
| The revolver and Term Loan A ended in May 2026; cash was USD 464.0 million at June 30, 2026. | Liquidity is cash only, with some held abroad. | High |

| The 2026 exchange moved secured maturities to July 2032, leaving USD 420.5 million of unsecured notes due first in February 2029. | Refinancing is deferred but ordered unfavourably; management says it depends on capital markets. | High |
| Buybacks of USD 30.0 million in six months 2026 were made under an amended covenant while earnings fell. | Cash is going to shareholders; limits sit in indentures not supplied. | Medium |
| A damages claim above USD 200 million was set for trial on October 27, 2026, with no outcome supplied. | A possible cash call that cannot be sized. | Medium |
### Credit view

AMC Global Media has a weakening but refinanced credit profile: it faces no debt maturity until February 2029, but its earnings are falling and its liquidity is now cash alone. The strongest support is cash generation, with USD 190.5 million of free cash flow in the twelve months to June 30, 2026 and cash of USD 464.0 million. The weakest point is earnings: adjusted operating income fell to USD 313.0 million from USD 411.9 million in FY2025, which lifted net debt to adjusted operating income to 4.06x from 3.10x while net debt was flat at USD 1,271.6 million, and the revolving credit facility no longer exists. The outcome depends on whether streaming growth and the Netflix licence cash offset linear decline before USD 420.5 million of unsecured notes fall due in February 2029.

Assessment: weakening, refinanced credit; category Analyst Interpretation; confidence Medium. The basis is the leverage, cover and liquidity figures [CP-1 C3, C4, C5, C11] and the business rows on revenue, control and transactions [CP-1A]. Confidence is below High because the business module judged this module ready only with limitations and listed unsupplied indentures as a high-severity gap.

Thesis: AMC Global Media has traded near-term maturity risk for a higher-cost, longer secured structure at the point its earnings are declining, so the credit now rests on stabilising earnings and cash generation rather than on committed back-up liquidity.
### Key findings

1. Earnings, not debt, drove the rise in leverage. Net debt moved from USD 1,275.9 million at December 31, 2025 to USD 1,271.6 million at June 30, 2026, while adjusted operating income over twelve months fell to USD 313.0 million from USD 411.9 million, taking net debt to adjusted operating income to 4.06x from 3.10x and total debt to adjusted operating income to 5.54x from 4.32x [CP-1 C3]. The fall came mainly from Domestic Operations, whose segment adjusted operating income was USD 61.0 million in Q2 2026 against USD 126.3 million in Q2 2025 as subscription, advertising and content licensing revenue all fell [CP-1 table; CP-1A operating model]. Management expects linear subscriber and advertising declines to continue, so the denominator carries more risk than the numerator.

2. Cash interest cover is thinner. Adjusted operating income covered cash interest paid 2.07x in the twelve months to June 30, 2026 against 2.63x in FY2025 [CP-1 C4]. Run-rate contractual coupon on the notes outstanding at June 30, 2026 is USD 156.0 million, which on the same earnings gives 2.01x [CP-1 C8]. On operating income plus depreciation and amortization with no add-backs, total debt is 12.66x earnings, but that basis includes a USD 97.8 million non-cash impairment and is shown only to expose the gap to the adjusted measure [CP-1 C7].

3. Liquidity is cash only. The company repaid the remaining Term Loan A and terminated the USD 175.0 million revolver on May 12, 2026, leaving cash of USD 464.0 million at June 30, 2026, of which about USD 136.5 million is held by foreign subsidiaries [CP-1 liquidity rows]. The unused USD 125.0 million receivables sale program is not a committed facility. This replaces a position where cash of USD 502.4 million was backed by USD 175.0 million undrawn at December 31, 2025.

4. The maturity profile is long but ordered against unsecured holders. After the March 2026 exchange, USD 420.5 million of 4.25% unsecured senior and convertible notes mature in February 2029 ahead of USD 1,315.1 million of 10.50% secured notes in July 2032 [CP-1 C11; CP-1A transactions]. Management states that cash and operating cash flow will not repay all debt at maturity and that it depends on capital markets access. Whether the 2032 indenture constrains refinancing the earlier notes is Insufficient Information.

5. Cash flow remains positive after capital spending, but is weaker. Free cash flow was USD 108.1 million in six months 2026 against USD 189.9 million in six months 2025, and USD 190.5 million over twelve months [CP-1 C5]. Debt principal has fallen by USD 633.8 million since December 31, 2024 [CP-1A calculations], largely through discounted repurchases, a tender and Term Loan A repayments.

6. Control and capital allocation matter to creditors. The Dolan family group owns all Class B stock and about 79% of voting power outside director elections, and the company bought back USD 30.0 million of stock in six months 2026 under an indenture amendment that allows up to USD 50.0 million of equity repurchases, with USD 87 million of board authorization remaining at June 30, 2026 [CP-1A governance]. Restricted payment capacity beyond the summarised amendment is Insufficient Information.

7. Two dated events sit after the balance sheet or before an unreported outcome. The Netflix licence of July 30, 2026 brings USD 500 million of fees, with management expecting about USD 25 million of cash in 2026 and about USD 100 million a year in 2027 to 2030; and a damages claim above USD 200 million had a trial set for October 27, 2026 with no outcome supplied [CP-1 subsequent events; CP-1A credit translations]. Neither is in June 30, 2026 balances, and both are limited by documents not supplied.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. First, the company has no debt maturing before February 2029 and its secured notes run to July 2032, after it exchanged USD 861.3 million of 2029 secured notes (tagged Documentary Fact; basis maturity rows and the 2026 transaction summary). Second, it generates cash: USD 190.5 million of free cash flow over twelve months to June 30, 2026 and cash of USD 464.0 million, with total debt principal USD 633.8 million lower than at December 31, 2024 (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1 C5 and CP-1A calculations). Third, it owns a large share of its scripted content and franchises, and has licensed the Walking Dead Universe to Netflix for USD 500 million of fees over five years; the licence terms are Management Language and the contract is not supplied (basis CP-1A operating model and subsequent events). Fourth, its documented behaviour towards debt has been supportive: it repurchased and tendered senior notes at discounts in 2025 and repaid its Term Loan A (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1A governance table). Fifth, reporting quality is high, with an unqualified audit opinion and effective internal control over financial reporting for FY2025 (Documentary Fact).

Weaknesses. First, earnings are falling: Q2 2026 revenue was USD 547.5 million against USD 600.0 million and operating income USD 15.9 million against USD 64.5 million, while operating cost lines rose (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1 table). Second, leverage and cover have weakened to 5.54x total and 4.06x net on adjusted operating income, and 2.07x cash interest cover (Analyst Interpretation of CP-1 C3 and C4; the adjusted measure adds back restructuring and share-based compensation). Third, there is no committed back-up facility, and the company states it depends on capital markets to refinance (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1 liquidity rows and CP-1A refinancing translation). Fourth, the earlier maturity is the junior one: USD 420.5 million of unsecured notes fall due in February 2029 ahead of the secured notes (Analyst Interpretation). Fifth, revenue is exposed to a few distributors and to advertising and subscriber declines that management expects to continue, and a customer filed for Chapter 11 on June 30, 2026 with exposure not stated (Documentary Fact for the filing; Insufficient Information for the exposure). Sixth, controlled equity, USD 30.0 million of buybacks and USD 87 million of authorization remaining while earnings fall (Documentary Fact; the creditor effect is Analyst Interpretation). Seventh, the unresolved damages claim above USD 200 million against cash of USD 464.0 million (Documentary Fact; the outcome is Insufficient Information). Eighth, ranking and collateral for the 2032 notes cannot be settled because the filing describes the guarantees as unsecured while the notes are secured by a first-priority lien (Insufficient Information; no recovery conclusion is drawn).
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Continued decline in linear affiliate and advertising revenue | Subscriber losses and ratings erosion reduce revenue while programming and marketing costs rose in Q2 2026, so adjusted operating income falls faster than revenue | Leverage rises further above 4.06x net and cash interest cover falls below 2.07x unless streaming and licensing offset | Critical |

| Refinancing of USD 420.5 million of unsecured notes due February 2029 | The earlier maturity is junior to the secured notes and the revolver is gone; management says it depends on capital markets access | Refinancing cost and access depend on earnings by 2028 | Material |

| Cash-only liquidity | USD 464.0 million cash, part held abroad, with no committed facility and USD 590.3 million of off-balance-sheet obligations | A cash shock, a litigation payment or a counterparty failure cannot be bridged by a facility | Material |

| Shareholder distributions under controlled ownership | Buyback capacity in the amended indenture and USD 87 million of authorization remaining; family control of the vote | Cash leaves the credit group instead of repaying debt; limits are in documents not supplied | Material |
| Litigation outcome | Claim above USD 200 million with trial set for October 27, 2026; no outcome supplied | A cash claim against cash of USD 464.0 million, unquantified | Material |

| Unseen documentation | Indentures, covenants for the surviving notes and the ranking wording are not supplied | Covenant headroom, restricted payment capacity and ranking cannot be assessed | Material |

| Counterparty and distributor concentration | A few distributors hold concentrated subscribers; a customer filed for Chapter 11 | Receivables of USD 547.2 million and renewal pricing are exposed; exposure to the filing customer unknown | Minor |
### Gaps
| Gap | Why it matters | Affects | Severity | Action |

| Indentures and security documents for the 2032, 4.25% senior and convertible notes not supplied | Restricted payments, debt incurrence, liens and ranking decide creditor control | Credit view, risks, strengths and weaknesses | High | Obtain the indentures and re-run the covenant and ranking review |

| No filing after July 30, 2026, although the as-of date is 2026-11-05 | The Q3 2026 position, the trial outcome and any refinancing are unknown | All findings | Medium | Add any later 10-Q or 8-K filed on or before 2026-11-05 |

| Ratings, market prices and peers not supplied | Market access and pricing of the 2029 refinancing cannot be judged; no relative statement is made | Refinancing risk | Medium | Add ratings and trading levels if available |
| Netflix agreement not supplied | Cash timing and termination terms are management expectations | Strength three and finding seven | Medium | Obtain the agreement or its summary |
| Identity and exposure of the customer in Chapter 11 not stated | Counterparty risk cannot be sized | Concentration risk | Low | Search later filings for the exposure |

| Covenant headroom at June 30, 2026 not calculable | Credit-agreement tests ended May 12, 2026; the surviving notes' tests are not printed | Credit view | High | Obtain covenant terms and compliance computation |
## Calculations

No new calculation. All ratios and amounts come from the financial base handoff (C3, C4, C5, C7, C8, C11) and the business handoff calculations, without recomputation. Unit conversions from USD thousands to USD millions used in the prose: total debt 1,735,554 is USD 1,735.6 million; net debt 1,271,558 is USD 1,271.6 million and 1,275,872 is USD 1,275.9 million; cash 463,996 is USD 464.0 million and 502,379 is USD 502.4 million; adjusted operating income 313,045 is USD 313.0 million and 411,874 is USD 411.9 million; free cash flow 190,523 is USD 190.5 million, 108,082 is USD 108.1 million and 189,926 is USD 189.9 million; 2029 maturities 420,456 is USD 420.5 million; 2032 maturities 1,315,098 is USD 1,315.1 million; run-rate coupon 155,955 is USD 156.0 million; debt principal reduction since December 31, 2024 of 633,831 is USD 633.8 million; revenue 547,495 and 600,024 are USD 547.5 million and USD 600.0 million; operating income 15,854 and 64,469 are USD 15.9 million and USD 64.5 million; Domestic segment adjusted operating income 60,972 and 126,339 are USD 61.0 million and USD 126.3 million; receivables 547,187 is USD 547.2 million; exchanged principal of about USD 861.3 million is from the business handoff; off-balance-sheet obligations of 590,300 are USD 590.3 million. Ratios quoted in x are copied from the financial base handoff at two decimals.
## Gaps

- Not supplied: executed indentures, security and guarantee documents, so restricted payment, incurrence and lien capacity are Insufficient Information and covenant headroom at June 30, 2026 is Not calculable.
- Not supplied: any filing after July 30, 2026, ratings, market prices, the Netflix agreement, and the identity and exposure of the customer in Chapter 11.
- Not disclosed in the pages searched: streaming churn, revenue per user and acquisition cost, so streaming durability is judged from reported subscriber totals and price increases only.
- Unresolved: whether the 2032 notes rank ahead of the 2029 unsecured notes in practice, given the filing's "unsecured basis" guarantee wording; no ranking or recovery conclusion is drawn.

- The adjusted operating income base is a company non-GAAP measure and not EBITDA; all leverage and cover ratios here carry that limit, and the reported-basis alternative is distorted by a one-time impairment.
- Upstream limitations L1 to L11 from the readiness handoff remain in force; the text-only extraction means figures should be rechecked at the cited page before external use.

Pass to CP-5 for evidence trace review: every figure here is a copy of a financial base value or a business handoff value, and the Management Language items (Netflix licence cash, expected declines, repurchase authorization) should be traced as attributed claims.
